question.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A=\{\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}+1}:n\in \{1,2,3,4\}\}.
$$

What is the supremum of $A?$

$sup(A)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The supremum of a set $A$ is the smallest upper bound of $A.$

If $A$ is a finite set, the supremum of $A$ equals its maximum. 

First, let's write down all the terms of our set by substituting $n=1,2,3,4$ into the expression for the elements of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(-1)^{1}}{(1)^{2}+1} & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{(-1)^{2}}{(2)^{2}+1} & =\frac{1}{5} \\ \frac{(-1)^{3}}{(3)^{2}+1} & =-\frac{1}{10} \\ \frac{(-1)^{4}}{(4)^{2}+1} & =\frac{1}{17}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
A=\{-\frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{5},\,-\frac{1}{10},\,\frac{1}{17}\}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}sup(A) & =max\{-\frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{5},\,-\frac{1}{10},\,\frac{1}{17}\}=\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
